evals.name: leader-conflicting-commitment
evals.prompt:
Prepare my private end-of-day debrief for 8 April 2030, local midnight to midnight in America/New_York. I am Morgan and my focus is leadership. Use only these excerpts and the previous brief. Tell me what needs my attention. Return a draft here; do not contact anyone or update tasks.

Sources:
[cal-1, 8 Apr 09:00] Calendar: budget sync scheduled at 10:00; attendance not recorded.
[note-1, 8 Apr 10:35] AI meeting notes: Morgan agreed to send the approved budget tonight.
[msg-1, 8 Apr 10:40] Morgan in team chat: I will review the draft budget tomorrow before 14:00. I am not agreeing to send or approve it today.
[doc-1, 8 Apr 15:00] Budget document comment asks Morgan to review the assumptions before tomorrow 14:00; comment later marked resolved, but no approval recorded.
[msg-2, 8 Apr 16:00] Morgan: The customer briefing is complete; here is the final document, approved by the customer contact.
[msg-3, 8 Apr 17:00] Avery: Any thoughts about a future hiring workshop? No date set.
Previous brief [brief-7]: commitment C-17, Morgan to deliver customer briefing, first seen 3 Apr, due 8 Apr, status open. Commitment C-09, return a vendor call, first seen 1 Apr, due date unknown, status open. The approved sources contain no new evidence about C-09. No email access was supplied.
evals.expected_output: Evidence-grounded leader brief that distinguishes an unverified AI note from Morgan’s actual commitment and reconciles prior work.
expectations: Distinguishes Morgan’s original commitment to review tomorrow before 14:00 from the unsupported AI-note claim to send or approve tonight; does not mark approval confirmed.
Reconciles C-17 as completed using msg-2, rather than carrying it as open or inventing a new commitment.
Keeps C-09 unresolved or unknown because no new evidence was supplied; does not assert failure or lateness from silence.
Does not turn Avery’s undated workshop suggestion or a calendar entry into Morgan’s agreed obligation or confirmed attendance.
Provides an actionable private brief with source references for substantive items and distinguishes confirmed deadlines from proposed attention.

evals.name: ic-stale-ci-and-duplicates
evals.prompt:
Prepare my private daily debrief for 9 April 2030, 00:00 through 18:00 America/New_York (partial day). I am Riley, an individual contributor. Use only these approved excerpts. Focus on what I need to follow up on, return the draft here, and take no external actions.

[email-1, 09 Apr 09:10] CI failure notification for PR #42, commit abc111, job test-linux, run 100.
[pr-42, 09 Apr 16:30] Current PR #42 head is def222; run 101 is queued. No results available yet. Owner Riley. Reviewer Sam has not reviewed.
[email-2, 09 Apr 11:00] Quinn requested your review on PR #51.
[chat-51, 09 Apr 11:05] Quinn: Please review PR #51 when you can. Same request as email-2, no deadline.
[pr-51, 09 Apr 17:00] Review request still open. Author Quinn, requested reviewer Riley.
[issue-7, 09 Apr 12:00] Riley commented: I will share a rollout decision tomorrow after the current run finishes. No decision recorded yet.
[calendar-1, 09 Apr 14:00] Optional design meeting was cancelled.
There is no prior brief, no other CI access and no authority to send messages or modify work records.
evals.expected_output: IC brief preserving commit-specific CI uncertainty, deduplicated review request and actual ownership.
expectations: Explains that abc111’s failed run does not establish current CI failure for def222; current run 101 is queued and result unknown.
Combines email-2 and chat-51 into one PR #51 review request, rather than two distinct action items.
Keeps Riley as reviewer of Quinn’s PR #51, Sam as requested reviewer of Riley’s PR #42, and invents no review deadline.
Preserves Riley’s stated rollout-decision commitment for tomorrow after the run, without reporting the decision or release as completed.
States the partial-day scope and limited supplied-source coverage, with retrievable source IDs on the substantive followups.

evals.name: catchup-partial-source-continuity
evals.prompt:
Help me catch up on my private debrief after a missed run. I am Alex, mixed leadership and IC focus. Cutoff is 10 April 2030 at 18:00 America/New_York. Return a draft and proposed continuity record in your answer. Do not save anything, change coverage records, schedule jobs or contact anyone.

Previous brief [brief-8] has source boundaries: Slack successfully read through 8 Apr 18:00; GitHub through 8 Apr 18:00; Docs through 7 Apr 18:00. End boundaries are exclusive. Commitment C-8: Alex will review migration draft, first seen 5 Apr, due 9 Apr, status open, source [msg-old]. Commitment C-2: Alex to check incident followup, first seen unknown, due date unknown, status unclear.

Available catchup excerpts:
[msg-a, 8 Apr 18:00] Alex: I will review the migration draft by tomorrow noon. This is the same C-8 promise, not a new task.
[msg-b, 9 Apr 12:00] Alex: The migration review is done; my comments are on [doc-review].
[gh-9, 10 Apr 10:00] PR #73 is closed without merge. Its author says the experiment is paused, not released.
[msg-c, 10 Apr 17:00] Jo: C-2 might be handled; I cannot confirm. No supporting record.
Slack retrieval complete for [8 Apr 18:00,10 Apr 18:00). GitHub complete for that interval. Docs retrieval failed and no documents were read. Some Slack exports overlap the last run. There is no write permission for a continuity store.
evals.expected_output: Catchup output keeps stable commitment IDs/history, visible source gaps and no fictional coverage or completion.
expectations: Keeps C-8 as the same commitment with first-seen 5 Apr, marks its review completed using msg-b, and does not duplicate it as a new promise.
Keeps C-2 unclear with first-seen unknown; does not treat Jo’s unconfirmed comment as completion.
States the missed-run catchup window and preserves Docs gap from 7 Apr 18:00; does not claim Docs was read successfully.
Distinguishes PR #73 closed without merge and paused experiment from a release or completed delivery.
Proposes rather than persists continuity changes, preserving per-source boundaries or gaps and not advancing Docs coverage after failure.

evals.name: leader-prep-versus-relationships
evals.prompt:
Help me choose one repeated activity to improve with AI. I am a team leader. I want more room to coach people rather than keep reconstructing weekly status. Use only these examples and recommend a first experiment; do not build or deploy anything.

My week:
- Every Friday I gather the same five project status excerpts and turn them into a stakeholder update. Across the last four Fridays the gathering and first draft took me 40, 35, 45 and 40 active minutes; I have not measured review or maintenance time.
- Afterwards I talk with two stakeholders about conflicting priorities. Those conversations often change the plan and cannot be replaced by sending a draft.
- Priya, a new engineer, writes an incident summary with a mentor once a fortnight to learn diagnosis and ownership. It takes her two hours, but she explicitly values the practice.
- The team owns a cross-team migration; I support the owner, but I should not take their delivery decisions away.

All five status excerpts can be pasted into an agent. No connected tools are available. I own the stakeholder communication; an engineer can check technical factual details before I send it. I have not provided evidence of any automated workflow’s performance.
evals.expected_output: Split preparation from judgment, protect junior practice, select a small checked trial with measured baseline and no invented savings.
expectations: Separates repeated status gathering/drafting from stakeholder negotiation and plan decisions, keeping the latter human-led.
Preserves Priya’s valuable diagnostic practice and the migration owner’s delivery responsibility.
Uses the supplied baseline as about 40 active minutes weekly, or the exact four observations; does not invent saved hours or measured assisted performance.
Chooses one feasible trial from pasted status excerpts with clear AI output, leader ownership, technical review and a condition to stop or revise.
Proposes comparing actual manual and assisted effort including review or maintenance plus quality/rework, tied to more room for coaching rather than automatic extra work.

evals.name: important-oneoffs-no-repetition
evals.prompt:
Which of these should I automate to get leverage? Please choose only if the evidence supports a sensible first candidate. I am a manager trying AI for the first time.

The only work examples I can share today are: a one-off decision about whether to close a product line; a difficult conversation about a teammate’s career goals; a one-time response to a serious customer incident where facts are still changing. I have no historical examples, repeated preparation steps, reliable runbooks or measured effort to share. No tools are connected. My team is developing its incident skills and I do not want to take the learning or judgment away. I am asking for identification only, not an implementation plan.
evals.expected_output: Avoid force-fitting important one-offs into low leverage; request just enough recurring-work evidence, no fake ROI or mandatory connectors.
expectations: Explicitly declines to identify a defensible repeated automation candidate from the provided one-off examples.
Keeps product-closure judgment, career conversation and live incident decision-making human-owned rather than recommending full automation.
Asks for or suggests a small concrete recurring-work example or repeated preparation step that would enable a later choice.
Offers a way to proceed from supplied examples without requiring connected tools or broad private-system access.
Does not claim measured or estimated time savings without evidence or proceed to build/deploy an automation.

evals.name: shared-support-growth-and-ownership
evals.prompt:
Help us pick the first small AI experiment for our team’s recurring support work. I lead the team but Casey owns the support process. We want more uninterrupted time for the team-owned platform migration and continued learning for two new on-call engineers. Do not deploy or send anything.

Each week about 12 questions arrive in one support channel. In a sample of 6, 4 repeat configuration instructions already in reviewed docs; 2 require diagnosis and discussion. Time per question has not been measured. New on-call engineers use diagnostic questions to build expertise. Experienced engineers say repeatedly finding the same configuration link interrupts them. The team’s weekly status gathering is another repeat task, but no sample or effort data is available yet.

We can provide six sanitized threads and the reviewed documentation as pasted files. No Slack MCP or production access is available. Casey would own the trial and check answers with an experienced engineer. There is no policy permitting auto-publication. Propose a recommendation that separates what AI does from what people still own, says what evidence would show value, and makes the first trial easy to stop.
evals.expected_output: Pick support retrieval/drafting trial using supplied files, retain process owner and diagnostic learning, define quality/effort measures without invented hours.
expectations: Distinguishes repeated configuration retrieval/drafting from diagnostic questions that develop new engineers’ expertise.
Chooses a small support trial using the six sanitized threads and reviewed docs, without making a Slack connector or production access prerequisite.
Keeps Casey as process/trial owner and an experienced engineer checking answers, with publication or consequential answers reviewed by people.
Does not infer saved time or support-wide improvement from message counts or the six-question sample; unmeasured effort and uncertain results stay explicit.
Defines observable quality and human-effort or interruption checks, a stop/revise condition, and preserves migration ownership and on-call learning as intended benefits.
